One Network. Many Servers. Shared AI Infrastructure.
Distributed local LLM inference engine pooling GPU VRAM and system RAM across LAN machines — powered by PyTorch, FastAPI, llama.cpp RPC, and native C++20 / MASM AVX2 SIMD kernels.


SHARD Distributed Inference Cluster: Central master coordinator pooling VRAM across connected LAN worker nodes over UDP discovery (:8001) and FastAPI SSE endpoints (:8000).

Overview · How It Works · Features · Quick Start · CLI Reference · Architecture · Dashboard · Community

What Is SHARD?

SHARD (shard-engine) is an open-source distributed local LLM inference engine written in Python (FastAPI + PyTorch) with a GGUF / llama.cpp backend and native C++20 / MASM AVX2 SIMD acceleration.

The Problem It Solves

Running capable 14B, 32B, or 70B+ open-weight language models locally typically hits a hard hardware wall: single-card VRAM limits. Most developers, labs, and small teams own multiple machines—a desktop gaming GPU, a workstation laptop, an auxiliary mini-PC—whose memory sits fragmented across the local network while no single device can fit the full model weights and KV cache.

Why SHARD Exists

SHARD unites idle GPUs and system memory across your Local Area Network (LAN) into a single logical inference cluster:

  • Pool Hardware Without Cloud Lock-In: Split transformer layers across multiple consumer GPUs and host RAM over standard gigabit LAN (lan.py, gguf_backend.py) with zero external cloud dependencies or recurring API fees.
  • Know Before You Download (shard fit): Inspect whether any Hugging Face model will fit your single GPU, hybrid CPU+GPU setup, or pooled LAN cluster before downloading gigabytes of weights (fit.py).
  • Drop-In Agent & IDE Backend: Expose both OpenAI (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/models) and Anthropic (/v1/messages) compatible endpoints on port 8000 so coding agents and SDKs connect immediately.

Who Should Use SHARD?

  • Local AI Developers & Researchers running 7B–70B GGUF or PyTorch SafeTensors models across home lab or office workstations.
  • Software Engineering Teams hosting private, zero-telemetry coding assistants for Cursor, Claude Code, Aider, Continue, Zed, and OpenCode.
  • AI Agent Builders orchestrating multi-agent pipelines via OpenAI Python SDK, LangChain, or LlamaIndex against self-hosted hardware.

How SHARD Works

SHARD turns distributed local AI infrastructure into a four-step workflow: CREATE → SHARE → CONNECT → USE.

1. CREATE — Launch Your Server

Start a local SHARD node with shard start or python main.py. The engine probes your CPU, system RAM, and NVIDIA CUDA / Apple MPS GPU via hardware.py, loads your chosen GGUF or Hugging Face model, and brings up the FastAPI server and Web UI on http://localhost:8000.

2. SHARE — Broadcast to the LAN

Open a LAN compute pool with shard lan create --open (or generate a pairing code via shard lan create). SHARD broadcasts UDP discovery beacons on port 8001 and exposes /api/lan/* endpoints so peer machines on your subnet can pool their VRAM and RAM.

3. CONNECT — Pair Worker Nodes

On any secondary computer on the network, run shard lan join <master-ip> --share. The worker completes an HTTP handshake (POST /api/lan/pair), launches its local RPC tensor worker, sends periodic health heartbeats, and contributes its GPU/RAM to the cluster.

4. USE — Power AI Agents & Apps

Connect coding IDEs, autonomous AI agents, or custom Python apps to http://<master-ip>:8000/v1/chat/completions or /v1/messages. Master coordinates layer execution across connected nodes and streams tokens back via Server-Sent Events (SSE).

Experimental Features

  • Multi-Host llama.cpp RPC Tensor Distribution (gguf_backend.py, lan.py): Distributed layer execution over TCP/RPC across heterogeneous LAN GPUs works best on low-latency wired Gigabit/2.5GbE Ethernet subnets; Wi-Fi links may experience higher inter-token latency.
  • Native Win32 Desktop GUI (native/shard_gui.cpp): Native C++ Windows desktop wrapper alongside the cross-platform web dashboard (dashboard.html).

Planned Features

  • Automated Dynamic Re-Sharding on Node Dropout: Seamless mid-generation layer migration if a worker node disconnects unexpectedly (docs/LAN_SHARDING_DESIGN.md).
  • Linux / macOS ARM64 NEON Intrinsics: Expanding the native SIMD kernel suite (native/) beyond x86-64 AVX2/FMA to native Apple Silicon / ARM64 assembly paths.

Installation & Quick Start

Prerequisites

  • OS: Windows 10/11 (64-bit), Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+ / Debian 12+), or macOS.
  • Python: Python 3.8+ (3.10+ recommended).
  • Hardware: NVIDIA GPU with CUDA drivers (recommended for GPU acceleration), Apple Silicon (MPS), or x86-64 CPU with AVX2 support.
  • Network (Optional for LAN Sharding): Two or more machines on the same LAN with TCP port 8000 (HTTP/API) and UDP/TCP port 8001 (LAN discovery & RPC) open.

Installation

Option 1: Install via PyPI (Recommended)

Install SHARD directly from PyPI in any environment:

# Core install: CLI, FastAPI server, web dashboard, GGUF (llama.cpp) + LAN clustering
pip install shard-engine

# Full install: adds PyTorch/Transformers safetensors & Hugging Face extras
pip install "shard-engine[full]"

To install the latest development snapshot directly from GitHub:

# Core install from GitHub
pip install "git+https://github.com/avelone123123/shard.git"

# Full install from GitHub
pip install "shard-engine[full] @ git+https://github.com/avelone123123/shard.git"

Verify your environment right after installation:

shard doctor

Windows PATH Note: If Windows reports that shard.exe is not on your PATH, you can run SHARD directly through Python: python -m shard_engine <command> (for example, python -m shard_engine help or python -m shard_engine start). GPU & Runtime Note: GGUF inference auto-downloads platform binaries for llama-server / ggml-rpc-server on first run and needs no extra ML packages. For CUDA PyTorch inference, install a matching CUDA build of torch before pip install "shard-engine[full]".

Option 2: Editable Install from Source (Developers)

git clone https://github.com/avelone123123/shard.git
cd shard
pip install -e ".[dev]"

Option 3: Docker Compose (with NVIDIA GPU Support)

git clone https://github.com/avelone123123/shard.git
cd shard
docker-compose up --build

This builds shard-engine, mounts persistent volumes (/data/models and /data/shard), exposes port 8000:8000, and enables NVIDIA GPU passthrough.

Option 4: Compile Native C++20 / MASM AVX2 Kernels (Optional Speedup)

To compile shard_core.dll (Windows MSVC cl.exe + ml64.exe) or shard_core.so (Linux GCC/Clang):

python native/build_native.py

Upgrading & Uninstalling

shard update --check
pip install --upgrade shard-engine
pip uninstall shard-engine

Uninstalling the Python package keeps your downloaded models, settings, and API keys intact in your user data directory.

Quick Start Workflow

1. Verify Environment & Launch SHARD

# Check Python runtime, dependencies, GPU VRAM, ports, and writable paths
shard doctor

# Start FastAPI server in background (--daemon / -d) and inspect logs/status
shard start --daemon
shard status

# Or open the interactive Web Dashboard at http://localhost:8000 immediately
shard gui

# Stop or restart background server cleanly
shard restart
shard stop

2. Check Hardware & Model Fit Before Downloading

# Check if a model fits your local machine or LAN cluster before downloading
shard fit Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct
shard fit meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct

3. Download & Run a Model

# Download and start an interactive terminal chat (default: Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct)
shard run Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct

# List cached and catalog models
shard list

4. Create or Join a Distributed LAN Cluster

On the Master Machine (shard lan create prints the live LAN IPv4 addresses detected on this host):

# Create an open LAN pool (auto-accepts subnet workers and sets target model)
shard lan create --open --share --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct

# Or create a code-protected LAN pool
shard lan create --share

On each Worker Machine on the same subnet, replace <SERVER_IP> with the IP printed by shard lan create on the Master Machine:

# Join an open LAN pool and contribute local GPU/RAM
shard lan join <SERVER_IP> --share

# Or join a code-protected pool
shard lan join <SERVER_IP> <PAIR_CODE> --share

# Inspect cluster nodes, host IPv4 addresses, and pooled VRAM/RAM
shard lan status

# Leave or disable LAN pooling
shard lan off

Cross-Platform Directories & Environment Variables (shard_engine/paths.py)

SHARD stores user data outside site-packages following OS conventions (and reads existing ~/.shard data cleanly on upgrade):

  • Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\SHARD (config, keys_db.json, logs/, run/, models/)
  • Linux: ~/.local/share/shard, ~/.config/shard, ~/.cache/shard, ~/.local/state/shard (respects XDG_* variables)
  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/SHARD, ~/Library/Caches/SHARD, ~/Library/Logs/SHARD
Variable / File Default Purpose
SHARD_HOST 0.0.0.0 Network interface IP address bound by server.py.
SHARD_PORT 8000 HTTP port for the API server and Web Dashboard.
SHARD_DATA_DIR OS data directory (/data/shard in Docker) Overrides root directory for settings.json, keys_db.json, lan.json, logs, and PID metadata.
SHARD_MODELS_DIR <data_dir>/models (/data/models in Docker) Storage directory for downloaded Hugging Face SafeTensors and GGUF weights.
SHARD_NO_BROWSER / SHARD_DOCKER (unset) Suppresses auto-opening a browser tab when starting SHARD.
SHARD_NATIVE_LIB (auto-discovered) Path override to shard_core.dll/.so/.dylib (set none to force Python fallback).
SHARD_SOUP_PYTHON / SHARD_SOUP_CMD (auto-discovered) Optional path to a Python 3.11–3.13 environment or binary running soup-cli when training on Python 3.14+ hosts.
HF_HOME / TRANSFORMERS_CACHE ~/.cache/huggingface Standard Hugging Face cache override respected by engine.py and hf_hub.py.
engine_optimizations.json Packaged inside shard_engine Runtime optimization profile loaded via importlib.resources.

Connecting AI Agents & Coding Tools

Point any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible client to your SHARD instance:

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1",
    api_key="shard-local",  # Or generate a token via `shard key --gen`
)

stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain tensor parallelism across LAN nodes."}],
    stream=True,
)

for chunk in stream:
    if chunk.choices[0].delta.content:
        print(chunk.choices[0].delta.content, end="", flush=True)

Distributed AI Cluster Mode

SHARD supports collaborative model-parallel execution across independent machines (LAN, Radmin VPN, Tailscale, WireGuard, or NAT-traversed encrypted tunnels). A coordinator can schedule a large model across multiple consented worker nodes and expose one unified OpenAI/Anthropic endpoint (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages).

Quick Start (Coordinator + Workers)

  1. Coordinator (Create & Publish Global Server):

    shard start --daemon
shard cluster create Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct --name MyGlobalCluster --strategy auto --publish --slots 4
shard cluster status

  2. Discover Global Servers & 1-Click Join:

    # Browse public catalog
shard cluster catalog --q deepseek --min-vram 16

# Join as an AI Consumer (Client):
shard cluster join shn_coordinator_node_id --client

# Join as a Compute Worker (Explicit Consent & Quota):
shard cluster join shn_coordinator_node_id --consent --vram-pct 70 --max-ram-gb 8 --max-threads 4

    For workers behind restrictive CGNAT/NAT, SHARD automatically traverses NAT using STUN or establishes an end-to-end ChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypted blind WebSocket relay tunnel with zero configuration.

  3. Deploy & Monitor:

    shard cluster plan
shard cluster deploy
shard cluster status

Supported Execution Backends & Documentation

  • GGUF Distributed RPC (gguf_rpc_layer_split): Splits model layers and KV cache across ggml-rpc-server workers and local offload devices via llama-server --rpc, with continuous batching (--parallel, --cont-batching).
  • PyTorch Pipeline Parallelism (torch_pipeline_parallel): Directly loads only assigned safetensors layer shards per worker (llama, qwen2, qwen3, mistral, gemma, gemma2, phi3, gpt2), maintains per-worker distributed KV caches, and streams binary tensor activations over authenticated SHPT TCP sockets.

USE — Power AI Agents & Apps Connect coding IDEs, autonomous AI agents, or custom Python apps to http://<master-ip>:8000/v1/chat/completions or /v1/messages. Master coordinates layer execution across connected nodes and streams tokens back via Server-Sent Events (SSE). Implemented Features Category Capability Source Module Description LAN Cluster & Sharding UDP Auto-Discovery & LAN Pooling lan.py, docs/LAN_SHARDING_DESIGN.md Broadcasts UDP beacons (:8001), pairs nodes via code or --open mode, monitors node heartbeats (/api/lan/heartbeat), and pools VRAM/RAM across machines. Inference Backends Dual PyTorch & GGUF (llama.cpp) Engine engine.py, gguf_backend.py Runs Hugging Face transformers / safetensors models on CUDA/CPU/MPS and quantized GGUF weights via managed llama-server & ggml-rpc-server subprocesses with configurable GPU layer offload (-ngl). Containerization Docker & NVIDIA GPU Compose Stack Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml Production-ready container setup with persistent named volumes (shard_models_volume, shard_data_volume) and NVIDIA GPU reservation. Native Win32 Desktop GUI (native/shard_gui.cpp): Native C++ Windows desktop wrapper alongside the cross-platform web dashboard (dashboard.html). Installation & Quick Start Prerequisites OS: Windows 10/11 (64-bit), Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+ / Debian 12+), or macOS. Python: Python 3.8+ (3.10+ recommended). Hardware: NVIDIA GPU with CUDA drivers (recommended for GPU acceleration), Apple Silicon (MPS), or x86-64 CPU with AVX2 support. Network (Optional for LAN Sharding): Two or more machines on the same LAN with TCP port 8000 (HTTP/API) and UDP/TCP port 8001 (LAN discovery & RPC) open. GPU & Runtime Note: GGUF inference auto-downloads platform binaries for llama-server / ggml-rpc-server on first run and needs no extra ML packages. For CUDA PyTorch inference, install a matching CUDA build of torch before pip install "shard-engine[full]". Option 2: Editable Install from Source (Developers) git clone https://github.com/avelone123123/shard.git cd shard pip install -e ".[dev]" Option 3: Docker Compose (with NVIDIA GPU Support) git clone https://github.com/avelone123123/shard.git cd shard docker-compose up --build This builds shard-engine, mounts persistent volumes (/data/models and /data/shard), exposes port 8000:8000, and enables NVIDIA GPU passthrough. Option 4: Compile Native C++20 / MASM AVX2 Kernels (Optional Speedup) To compile shard_core.dll (Windows MSVC cl.exe + ml64.exe) or shard_core.so (Linux GCC/Clang): python native/build_native.py Upgrading & Uninstalling shard update --check pip install --upgrade shard-engine pip uninstall shard-engine Uninstalling the Python package keeps your downloaded models, settings, and API keys intact in your user data directory. One Network. Many Servers. Shared AI Infrastructure. Distributed local LLM inference engine pooling GPU VRAM and system RAM across LAN machines — powered by PyTorch, FastAPI, llama.cpp RPC, and native C++20 / MASM AVX2 SIMD kernels.

SHARD Distributed Inference Cluster: Central master coordinator pooling VRAM across connected LAN worker nodes over UDP discovery (:8001) and FastAPI SSE endpoints (:8000).

Overview · How It Works · Features · Quick Start · CLI Reference · Architecture · Dashboard · Community

What Is SHARD?

SHARD (shard-engine) is an open-source distributed local LLM inference engine written in Python (FastAPI + PyTorch) with a GGUF / llama.cpp backend and native C++20 / MASM AVX2 SIMD acceleration.

The Problem It Solves

Running capable 14B, 32B, or 70B+ open-weight language models locally typically hits a hard hardware wall: single-card VRAM limits. Most developers, labs, and small teams own multiple machines—a desktop gaming GPU, a workstation laptop, an auxiliary mini-PC—whose memory sits fragmented across the local network while no single device can fit the full model weights and KV cache.

Why SHARD Exists

SHARD unites idle GPUs and system memory across your Local Area Network (LAN) into a single logical inference cluster:

  • Pool Hardware Without Cloud Lock-In: Split transformer layers across multiple consumer GPUs and host RAM over standard gigabit LAN (lan.py, gguf_backend.py) with zero external cloud dependencies or recurring API fees.
  • Know Before You Download (shard fit): Inspect whether any Hugging Face model will fit your single GPU, hybrid CPU+GPU setup, or pooled LAN cluster before downloading gigabytes of weights (fit.py).
  • Drop-In Agent & IDE Backend: Expose both OpenAI (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/models) and Anthropic (/v1/messages) compatible endpoints on port 8000 so coding agents and SDKs connect immediately.

Who Should Use SHARD?

  • Local AI Developers & Researchers running 7B–70B GGUF or PyTorch SafeTensors models across home lab or office workstations.
  • Software Engineering Teams hosting private, zero-telemetry coding assistants for Cursor, Claude Code, Aider, Continue, Zed, and OpenCode.
  • AI Agent Builders orchestrating multi-agent pipelines via OpenAI Python SDK, LangChain, or LlamaIndex against self-hosted hardware.

How SHARD Works

SHARD turns distributed local AI infrastructure into a four-step workflow: CREATE → SHARE → CONNECT → USE.

1. CREATE — Launch Your Server Start a local SHARD node with shard start or python main.py. The engine probes your CPU, system RAM, and NVIDIA CUDA / Apple MPS GPU via hardware.py, loads your chosen GGUF or Hugging Face model, and brings up the FastAPI server and Web UI on http://localhost:8000. 2. SHARE — Broadcast to the LAN Open a LAN compute pool with shard lan create --open (or generate a pairing code via shard lan create). SHARD broadcasts UDP discovery beacons on port 8001 and exposes /api/lan/* endpoints so peer machines on your subnet can pool their VRAM and RAM.
3. CONNECT — Pair Worker Nodes On any secondary computer on the network, run shard lan join <master-ip> --share. The worker completes an HTTP handshake (POST /api/lan/pair), launches its local RPC tensor worker, sends periodic health heartbeats, and contributes its GPU/RAM to the cluster. 4. USE — Power AI Agents & Apps Connect coding IDEs, autonomous AI agents, or custom Python apps to http://<master-ip>:8000/v1/chat/completions or /v1/messages. Master coordinates layer execution across connected nodes and streams tokens back via Server-Sent Events (SSE).

Installation & Quick Start

先决条件

  • OS: Windows 10/11 (64-bit), Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+ / Debian 12+), or macOS.
  • Python: Python 3.8+ (3.10+ recommended).
  • Hardware: NVIDIA GPU with CUDA drivers (recommended for GPU acceleration), Apple Silicon (MPS), or x86-64 CPU with AVX2 support.
  • Network (Optional for LAN Sharding): Two or more machines on the same LAN with TCP port 8000 (HTTP/API) and UDP/TCP port 8001 (LAN discovery & RPC) open.

安装

Option 1: Install via PyPI (Recommended)

Install SHARD directly from PyPI in any environment:

# Core install: CLI, FastAPI server, web dashboard, GGUF (llama.cpp) + LAN clustering
pip install shard-engine

# Full install: adds PyTorch/Transformers safetensors & Hugging Face extras
pip install "shard-engine[full]"

To install the latest development snapshot directly from GitHub:

# Core install from GitHub
pip install "git+https://github.com/avelone123123/shard.git"

# Full install from GitHub
pip install "shard-engine[full] @ git+https://github.com/avelone123123/shard.git"

Verify your environment right after installation:

shard doctor
Windows PATH Note: If Windows reports that shard.exe is not on your PATH, you can run SHARD directly through Python: python -m shard_engine <command> (for example, python -m shard_engine help or python -m shard_engine start). GPU & Runtime Note: GGUF inference auto-downloads platform binaries for llama-server / ggml-rpc-server on first run and needs no extra ML packages. For CUDA PyTorch inference, install a matching CUDA build of torch before pip install "shard-engine[full]".

Option 2: Editable Install from Source (Developers)

git clone https://github.com/avelone123123/shard.git
cd shard
pip install -e ".[dev]"

Option 3: Docker Compose (with NVIDIA GPU Support)

git clone https://github.com/avelone123123/shard.git
cd shard
docker-compose up --build

This builds shard-engine, mounts persistent volumes (/data/models and /data/shard), exposes port 8000:8000, and enables NVIDIA GPU passthrough.

Option 4: Compile Native C++20 / MASM AVX2 Kernels (Optional Speedup)

To compile shard_core.dll (Windows MSVC cl.exe + ml64.exe) or shard_core.so (Linux GCC/Clang):

python native/build_native.py

Upgrading & Uninstalling

shard update --check
pip install --upgrade shard-engine
pip uninstall shard-engine

Uninstalling the Python package keeps your downloaded models, settings, and API keys intact in your user data directory.

Quick Start Workflow

1. Verify Environment & Launch SHARD

# Check Python runtime, dependencies, GPU VRAM, ports, and writable paths
shard doctor

# Start FastAPI server in background (--daemon / -d) and inspect logs/status
shard start --daemon
shard status

# Or open the interactive Web Dashboard at http://localhost:8000 immediately
shard gui

# Stop or restart background server cleanly
shard restart
shard stop

2. Check Hardware & Model Fit Before Downloading

# Check if a model fits your local machine or LAN cluster before downloading
shard fit Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct
shard fit meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct

3. Download & Run a Model

# Download and start an interactive terminal chat (default: Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct)
shard run Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct

# List cached and catalog models
shard list

4. Create or Join a Distributed LAN Cluster

On the Master Machine (shard lan create prints the live LAN IPv4 addresses detected on this host):

# Create an open LAN pool (auto-accepts subnet workers and sets target model)
shard lan create --open --share --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct

# Or create a code-protected LAN pool
shard lan create --share

On each Worker Machine on the same subnet, replace <SERVER_IP> with the IP printed by shard lan create on the Master Machine:

# Join an open LAN pool and contribute local GPU/RAM
shard lan join <SERVER_IP> --share

# Or join a code-protected pool
shard lan join <SERVER_IP> <PAIR_CODE> --share

# Inspect cluster nodes, host IPv4 addresses, and pooled VRAM/RAM
shard lan status

# Leave or disable LAN pooling
shard lan off

Distributed AI Cluster Mode

SHARD supports collaborative model-parallel execution across independent machines (LAN, Radmin VPN, Tailscale, WireGuard, or NAT-traversed encrypted tunnels). A coordinator can schedule a large model across multiple consented worker nodes and expose one unified OpenAI/Anthropic endpoint (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages).

Quick Start (Coordinator + Workers)

  1. Coordinator (Create & Publish Global Server): shard start --daemon shard cluster create Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct --name MyGlobalCluster --strategy auto --publish --slots 4 shard cluster status
  2. Discover Global Servers & 1-Click Join: # Browse public catalog shard cluster catalog --q deepseek --min-vram 16 # Join as an AI Consumer (Client): shard cluster join shn_coordinator_node_id --client # Join as a Compute Worker (Explicit Consent & Quota): shard cluster join shn_coordinator_node_id --consent --vram-pct 70 --max-ram-gb 8 --max-threads 4 For workers behind restrictive CGNAT/NAT, SHARD automatically traverses NAT using STUN or establishes an end-to-end ChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypted blind WebSocket relay tunnel with zero configuration.
